So you're a newfag who wants to build a computer but don't know where to start? This guide is for you! We'll go over the basic part selection, recommended parts for each range, and I'll even teach you how to wipe your ass!

The best place for finding the place with the cheapest parts is a little site called pcpartpicker.com. They support several countries (Australia, Canada, Germany, Spain, Italy, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and the USA) and will help you find the cheapest version of any computer part that's for sale with major retailers with your country. They think so that you can use your brain for more important stuff like finding the fucking camper in Cawwadoody and Butterfingers 4.

We're going to build a couple example PCs in this guide so you can get a feel for it, you massive vagina.

Let's start with the CPU.

If you're a poorfag, get an Intel Core i3-4170. It has a mediocre 2 cores at 3.7GHz. It's not amazing, but it'll play your shitty games, and also less shitty ones like Civilization and Fallout 4. If you're not a massive cheapskate, you'd want something better, like an Intel Core i5-4690K. The K stands for unlocKed, meaning you can overclock it, which means you can make it go faster if you're not an idiot. But you're new which means you won't be doing that. The only reason AMD is around is so Intel doesn't get prosecuted by the United States Department of Justice for anticompetitive activites.

Additional: If you're too poor to afford a GPU, get an Intel Core i5-5675C. Why, you ask? Because it completely blows away any low end graphics cards (GPUs).

Okay now that you have the brain of your computer, it's already smarter than you and it doesn't even have a body yet. Let's get to fixing that? What we're getting next is the motherboard.

I hope it loves you more than your own mother did.

How to buy a motherboard:

If you're buying a K CPU (remember the previous section!) you want to get a motherboard chipset that starts with a Z (for Zuperfast), pcpartpicker will only show you motherboards that your CPU can be plugged into so again, you don't have to think! The current (as of June 21st, 2015, idiot) Z(uperfast) chipset is the Z97, and it is for Socket LGA1150. LGA means Land Grid Array, which means the CPU pins are on the motherboard, not the CPU. So be careful putting the CPU in, sausage fingers. You'll ruin the motherboard if you aren't and the motherboard manufacturers will laugh at you if you try to RMA it. If you're buying a poorfag CPU like an i3, you want to get H97. It's cheaper, can't overclock CPUs, and looks uglier. But you don't care about any of that because you aren't going to be overclocking an i3.

The big 4 motherboard manufacturers (in no particular order): ASUS (pronounced eh-soose because they're massive nerds), ASRock, Gigabyte, MSI. Intel used to make motherboards but stopped because they were terrible. EVGA makes a few niche motherboards and they're expensive as fuck.

How to choose a motherboard:

Is it from one of the big 4? No? It's garbage. Try again. Choose a motherboard that has at least 1 PCIe 16x slot (it's the big long slot that looks like you could stick a credit card in it [don't]), is the right CPU socket for your CPU (LGA1150 CPUs only go in LGA1150 boards, and so on), and has enough RAM slots (either 2 or 4) for what you have. If the rating is very low on pcpp (and it has more than 2 reviews), double check with the subverse before buying it.

You're probably thinking at this point that the motherboard section was all over the place. I don't give a shit. Read it again. Pop quiz!

How do you know if the motherboard is compatible?
Which board do you buy if you don't need to overclock?
What's a PCIe 16x slot?
Do you know how to triforce?

Time to move on.

RAM!

How to buy RAM: Sort by price, choose the cheapest 2x4GB set that's on pcpartpicker.com. You're done, time to move on.

Graphics Cards.

These are fun, they let you see what you're doing in the latest Cawwadoody and Butterfingers, and also let you watch movies and download pictures of lolis. Buying a Graphics Card is a bit more complicated than a CPU, motherboard, or RAM. If you went the i5-5765C route and are choosing to use on-board graphics, you can skip this section. See you in the next section nerd.

There is an extremely large range of GPUs, and it changes often. Anything I type in this guide will be out of date by the Fall.

So let's do some general stuff. For a Graphics Card, your minimum budget is going to be $150. Low end graphics cards will range from $150-$200. Middle of the road will be $200+. High end will be $300+. Extreme is $600+. Spending more burger tokens will make your FPS higher, and let you set the graphics higher. The GPU will always be the largest part of your computer budget, and you should never spend more on the CPU than on the Graphics Card. If you want to buy a $300 CPU you shouldn't be buying a $175 graphics card. It's like having big head mode on in Goldfinger. Don't go the other way either, you don't want your computer to be a brainless meathead. Think of the graphics card as muscles and the CPU as brains. Get a good balance of both. As of June 21st, there's a lot of good GPUs out. My current recommended as of June 21:

  • Extreme: 980 Ti. Currently retails for US$650 or so.
  • Upper High End: GeForce 980 retails for US$483.
  • High End: AMD Radeon R9 290X retails for US$304. nvidia's GeForce 970 retails for US$314.
  • Middle of the Road: GeForce 960, AMD Radeon R9 280X both cost approximately $200 and are quality cards.
  • Low End: AMD Radeon R9 280 is the lowest end card I can in good faith recommend. Everything below it is just hot garbage, and it's not exactly expensive, cheapest is $150 and will be better than the on-board of the i5-5765C.

In conclusion on Graphics Cards, in order of most expensive to least:

  • GeForce 980 Ti
  • GeForce 980
  • GeForce 970
  • Radeon R9 290X
  • Radeon R9 280X
  • GeForce 960
  • Radeon R9 280

Other cards will be introduced over time and your best bet is to research for current information.

Power Supplies!

They're scary zappy things that shouldn't be opened, and take your wall power and convert it from 120/220V to the 12V, 5V, and 3.3V that your computer uses. The number 1 manfacturer of Power Supplies is a company called Seasonic. If you can afford the Seasonic in your budget, get it.

My wattage recommendations change based on how many graphics cards you have. Yes kiddies, you can have more than 1 graphics card, for the small small price of massive fucking headaches all the time and games randomly crashing.

  • No Graphics Card: 400W.
  • 1 GPU: 550W-600W.
  • 2 GPU: 800W.
  • 3 GPU: 900W.
  • 4 GPU: 1000W+

Modular Power Supplies mean you only need to plug in the cables you need to run your system, and don't have an octopus hiding inside the case. They also cost more. Besides Seasonic, Corsair, XFX, Rosewill, and Fractal Design make good Power Supplies. Do not buy Diablotek, Logisys, or Topower under ANY circumstances. They will catch fire, or ruin your system. DO NOT CHEAP OUT ON YOUR POWER SUPPLY.

Hard Drives!

They hold your porn, your video games, your shitty romance novels, and other things.

How to buy a hard drive:

Sort by cheapest per gigabyte on pcpartpicker. Choose a hard drive that's 2 Terabytes. Make sure it isn't a WD Purple. Seasonic are usually cheaper. There are 4 relavent Hard Drive manufacturers: Seasonic, Western Digital (WD), Hitachi, and oddly enough, Toshiba. All drives are about the same reliability, with a few exceptions. There are certain dud models that should be avoided, and as long as you post your build on Voat first, you'll generally avoid that pitfall, assuming you were too lazy to research you fat fuck. More terabytes means you can store more things. You can have as many hard drives as you have SATA slots on your motherboard. If you think you'll need more than 2TB, choose a larger drive, dumpass.

Solid State Drives!

They're basically magic. You know those little USB flash drives that you can use to transfer data? These are like that except 10x bigger and about 500x faster. They're like taking a normal computer and applying black magic to it. Your OS boot time will drop down to 15 seconds (or less!). and everything installed on them will be faster. SSDs experience something called media wear, as instead of magnetic discs spinning at 5400-7200RPM inside the drive, it's flash memory. Flash memory can only take a limited amount of reads/writes until they fail. How many? This tells you how many it can take. I'd highly recommend all of the drives reviewed there, and they are extremely reliable as shown.

Case:

It's a metal box your parts go in. There's lots of different good cases, for all sorts of idiots, even you. Some good players in this market: Fractal Design, Corsair (sails = sales!), BitFenix, ThermalTake, Antec, Azza, Cougar, and Apevia. Choose a case that looks nice and will hold all your worthless garbage.

CPU Cooler:

Why is this at the end? Because fuck you that's why. Don't be a bitch. The CPU cooler keeps your CPU from melting. That's good. CPUs that aren't cooled properly fail. That's bad. You don't want that. Hyper 212 is the most recommended cooler. If you don't care about looks, just buy it. If you want water cooling instead of air cooling, read on.

Core 2 process
